chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the funerals of men and women when they are gathered together, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The men are preceded [in burial], as it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali (a reference to a legal text attributed to Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the order of burial for men and women according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the precedence of men over women in funeral processions, grounding the ruling in the 'Book of Ali' (*Kitab Ali*), which likely refers to a specific legal compilation or authoritative text attributed to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential tradition of linking practical legal rulings (*ahkam*) to the teachings and written works of the Imams, emphasizing the continuity of legal authority from the Prophet's household.
